# Presen'it! — guide for LLMs

> Turn a normal Markdown document into polished presentation slides and PDF with minimal directives.

Package: `@axt_ayakoto/presenit` (npm)
CLI: `presenit`

## Mental model

1. Author **one** Markdown file: `src/<slug>/slide.md`
2. It should remain readable as a normal Markdown document
3. Split pages/columns with HTML comment directives only
4. Do **not** invent JSX, custom HTML layouts, or extra config files

## Project layout

```text
src/<slug>/slide.md
src/<slug>/assets/...   # optional images
dist/<slug>/view.html   # from `presenit build`
dist/<slug>/resume.pdf  # from `presenit export`
```

## Commands

```bash
pnpm add -D @axt_ayakoto/presenit
pnpm exec presenit dev <slug>
pnpm exec presenit build <slug>
pnpm exec presenit export <slug>
```

## Frontmatter (YAML)

```yaml
---
theme: dark          # light | dark (default: light)
hue: 210             # number, mod 360 (default: 210)
width: 1920          # px (default: 1920)
height: 1080         # px (default: 1080)
fontSize: 32         # px
fontFamily:
  sans: '"M PLUS 1", system-ui, sans-serif'
  mono: '"M PLUS 1 Code", ui-monospace, monospace'
pageTransition:
  type: fade             # none | fade | scroll (default: fade; ignored in PDF)
  duration: 0.2          # seconds (default: 0.2)
rawHTML: false       # true only if you intentionally embed HTML
---
```

Unknown keys are ignored. Wrong types fall back to defaults with warnings.

`fontFamily.sans` / `.mono` accept a CSS stack string **or** a YAML/JSON array of family names
(e.g. `sans: ["Edu VIC WA NT Hand", "Zen Kurenaido", cursive]`). Spaced names are quoted in CSS automatically.
Named families (not generics like `serif` / `system-ui`) are requested from Google Fonts automatically;
locally installed fonts still take priority in the browser.

## Directives

Only these HTML comments, alone between blocks:

```html
<!-- presen-it! slide-break -->
<!-- presen-it! column-break -->
<!-- presen-it! slide-break (center-x=true) -->
<!-- presen-it! column-break (center-x=true&center-y=false) -->
```

Rules:
- Commands: `slide-break`, `column-break`
- Options: `center-x=true|false`, `center-y=true|false`
- No spaces around `=` or `&`
- Defaults: `center-x=false`, `center-y=true`
- Column options override slide options
- Unknown command/option → warning and ignore directive

### Page structure

- Content before the first `slide-break` is page 1
- A leading `slide-break` at file top applies options to page 1 (no empty page)
- Leading `h2` after a slide-break becomes the page header
- To keep an `h2` in the body, put `column-break` immediately after `slide-break`
- Empty columns are removed
- Trailing non-directive HTML comment = speaker notes (presenter only)

## Supported Markdown extras

- GFM (tables, strikethrough, task lists, etc.); task lists (`- [ ]` / `- [x]`) render as read-only checkboxes
- Code fences → Shiki highlight
- ` ```mermaid ` → SVG via beautiful-mermaid
- `$inline$` and `$$ block $$` math → KaTeX

## Writing tips for high-quality slides

- Prefer short bullets; one idea per slide
- Use `center-x=true` for title / quote / single figure slides
- Use columns for text + figure
- Keep speaker notes factual and short
- Avoid raw HTML unless `rawHTML: true` is intentional

## Example

```md
---
theme: dark
hue: 210
---

# Title

Subtitle

<!-- presen-it! slide-break -->

## Section

- Point A
- Point B

<!-- note for the speaker -->

<!-- presen-it! slide-break (center-x=true) -->

## Diagram

\`\`\`mermaid
graph LR
  A --> B
\`\`\`
```

## Viewer keys

- `←` `→` / Space: navigate
- `Home` `End`: first/last
- Projection short-press zones: left 10% = previous, right 10% = next (ignores drag / text selection; hover shows a chevron affordance)
- Bottom-left hover toolbar: Overview / Presenter / Fullscreen
- `O`: overview grid
- `F`: fullscreen
- `P`: presenter mode
- `T`: timer pause/resume (presenter)
- URL hash `#N` (1-based) syncs the current page (kept across markdown reload in `dev`)
- `?presenter` query: open presenter directly
- Sample gallery: `pnpm presenit dev kitchen-sink`
